text:
Bitcoin consolidated in the $62,500–$63,100 range on Sunday, July 5, sustaining its recovery from the July 2 low of $57,750. While the Fear & Greed Index remains deep in "extreme fear" territory at 15/100, contrarian institutional buying has begun stabilizing the market. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs broke their eighth consecutive week of net outflows on the final trading day of the week, logging a $221.7 million net inflow led by Fidelity's FBTC.

In traditional finance, macro assets remain frozen over the weekend with the DXY holding its post-payroll retreat at 100.86 and the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.49%. Equity futures point to a neutral start to the week as traders look forward to the July 8 FOMC minutes and the July 14 CPI inflation print. This macro calm has allowed digital assets to digest the recent short squeeze and establish a firmer structure above $62,000.
